trapHints: \(f''>0\) is a MINIMUM, not a maximum: Second-derivative test: at a critical point \(f''>0\) means the curve is concave up ⇒ a local minimum; \(f''<0\) ⇒ a local maximum. The sign is the opposite of what students often guess. (\(f''=0\) is inconclusive — fall back to the first-derivative test.)

\(f'=0\) is NECESSARY, not sufficient, for an extremum: A critical point is only a CANDIDATE. \(f'=0\) can be a point of inflection with no extremum (e.g. \(f(x)=x^3\) at \(x=0\)). You must still confirm a genuine sign change of \(f'\) (or check \(f''\)).

stem: Cubic has no extremum when its \(f'\) (a quadratic) has?
trapHints: Count genuine SIGN-CHANGES of \(f'\), not just roots of \(f'\): A root of \(f'\) is an extremum only if \(f'\) actually flips sign there. A repeated root (e.g. \(f'=(x-2)^2\)) touches zero without changing sign — no extremum. For a cubic to have NO extremum, force \(f'\) (a quadratic) to have discriminant \(<0\) so it never changes sign.
